react to criticism: Good leaders react to criticism calmly and use it to improve, instead of getting angry at people.
好的領導者會冷靜地對批評作出反應，並用它來改進，而不是對人生氣。
react against tradition: Many young artists react against tradition by using bright colors and strange shapes in their paintings.
許多年輕藝術家以在畫作中使用鮮豔色彩和奇特形狀來反抗傳統。
react with anger: Many fans reacted with anger to the team's sudden decision to sell its star player.
許多球迷對球隊突然決定賣掉明星球員一事憤怒反應。
chemicals react: When these two chemicals react, they produce heat and a strong smell, so do the experiment carefully.
當這兩種化學物質起反應時，會產生熱和強烈的氣味，所以做實驗要小心。
read between the lines: Her letter sounded cheerful, but if you read between the lines, you could tell she was lonely.
她的信聽起來很開朗，但如果你領會言外之意，就能看出她很寂寞。
read one's mind: You must have read my mind, because I was just about to order the same chocolate dessert!
你一定看穿了我的心思，因為我正要點同樣的巧克力甜點！
read the signs: Experienced sailors can read the signs in the sky and know when a storm is coming.
有經驗的水手能從天空看出徵兆，知道暴風雨何時來臨。
read a situation: A good leader can read a situation quickly and judge what the people around her really need.
好的領導者能迅速判斷情勢，並判斷身邊的人真正需要什麼。
read for a degree: After working for five years, my aunt went back to university to read for a degree in law.
工作五年後，我阿姨回到大學攻讀法律學位。
read into: Don't read too much into his short reply; he was probably just busy with work today.
別過度解讀他簡短的回覆；他今天可能只是忙於工作。
read someone's lips: The room was so noisy that I had to read my friend's lips to understand what she was saying.
房間太吵了，我必須讀朋友的唇才能明白她在說什麼。
reap the benefits: If you exercise regularly now, you will reap the benefits of good health when you are older.
如果你現在規律運動，等你年紀大了就會收穫健康的好處。
reap rewards: Students who study hard all year will reap rewards when the exam results finally come out.
整年用功讀書的學生在考試成績公布時會獲得回報。
reap what you sow: If you are always rude to others, you will reap what you sow and end up with no friends.
如果你總是對別人無禮，你就會自食其果，最後一個朋友也沒有。
reap profits: The company reaped profits from its new game, which sold millions of copies around the world.
這家公司從新遊戲中賺取利潤，這款遊戲在全世界賣出了數百萬套。
reap a harvest: After months of hard work in the fields, the farmers were happy to reap a harvest of golden rice.
在田裡辛苦工作幾個月後，農夫們很高興能收成金黃的稻米。
rear children: My grandparents worked hard on their farm to rear children and send all five of them to school.
我的祖父母在農場辛勤工作，養育小孩，並讓五個孩子都去上學。
rear its ugly head: Just when the town thought the problem was solved, air pollution reared its ugly head again.
就在小鎮以為問題已經解決時，空氣污染的醜陋面貌又再度浮現。
rear cattle: His family has reared cattle on this land for three generations, selling milk and beef in town.
他家三代以來都在這片土地上養牛，在鎮上賣牛奶和牛肉。
bring up the rear: The teacher walked at the front of the line, and the class leader brought up the rear so no one got lost.
老師走在隊伍最前面，班長則殿後，以免有人走失。
reason with someone: I tried to reason with my little brother and explain why sharing was fair, but he refused to listen.
我試著跟弟弟講理，解釋為什麼分享才公平，但他不肯聽。
reason that: She reasoned that if she saved 100 dollars a week, she could buy the new bike in two months.
她推論，如果每週存一百元，兩個月後就能買那輛新腳踏車。
it stands to reason: It stands to reason that if you sleep only four hours, you will feel tired the next day.
如果你只睡四個小時，隔天會覺得累是理所當然的。
reason out: Instead of asking the teacher right away, try to reason out the answer by yourself first.
與其馬上問老師，不如先試著自己推理出答案。
listen to reason: My father wouldn't listen to reason and drove through the storm even though we begged him to wait.
我爸爸不聽勸，即使我們求他等一等，他還是冒著暴風雨開車。
within reason: You can invite friends to the party within reason, but please don't bring more than ten people.
你可以在合理範圍內邀朋友來派對，但請不要帶超過十個人。
reassure the public: The government held a press conference to reassure the public that the tap water was safe to drink.
政府召開記者會安撫大眾，表示自來水可以安全飲用。
reassure someone that: The doctor reassured my mother, who had never heard of this surgery before, that it was simple and safe.
醫生向從未聽過這種手術的媽媽保證，手術既簡單又安全。
feel reassured: After talking with her teacher about the exam, Amy felt reassured and slept well that night.
和老師談過考試的事之後，艾咪感到安心，那晚睡得很好。
a reassuring smile: The nurse gave the frightened child a reassuring smile before giving him the shot.
打針前，護士給了那個害怕的孩子一個令人安心的微笑。
